1.x: The **Samaveda** is **compiled from the Rigveda**: about 1,549 verses (1,875 with repeats), all but about 75 from the Rigveda (mostly Mandalas VIII and IX).

**Atharvaveda:** the earliest charms and spells; **Ayurveda ("Science of Life") first appears** here (its prime origin); the term **kshetra-patni ("mistress of the field")** originates here; the Sabha and Samiti = "twin daughters of **Prajapati**"; mentions Pashupati; recensions **Paippalada, Shaunaka**; reflects non-Aryan beliefs.
**Trayi / Vedatrayi** = **Rig, Yajur, Sama**; the Atharvaveda was excluded (recognised later).
The **Yajurveda** has two branches, **Krishna (Black)** and **Shukla (White)**; it first mentions the Rajasuya and Vajapeya.
**Upavedas:** Ayurveda – medicine; Dhanurveda – warfare; Gandharvaveda – music; **Shilpaveda – architecture**.
Vedic people were skilled in **astronomy** (Vedanga Jyotisha), **mathematics** (Sulbasutra geometry) and **medicine** (Atharvaveda) – **not chemistry**.
Hotri, Adhvaryu, Udgatri, Brahman = Rig, Yajur, Sama, Atharva; the Trayi excludes the Atharva.

2.x: **108** (Muktika list), about **13 principal**; c. 800–600 BCE; **anti-ritualistic**; **Atman = Brahman**; karma, samsara, moksha; called **Vedanta** ("end of the Vedas").
**Prasthanatrayi** = the **Upanishads, Brahma Sutra** (Badarayana) and **Bhagavad Gita**; the **Bhagavata is not** included. **Shankaracharya** wrote bhashyas on these three – **not on the Rigveda**.

Satyameva Jayate = **Mundaka** (not Mandukya); the Jabala Upanishad is a different, later text.
